subject.title: [Feature]: Cloud Relay — openclaw login + heartbeat + relay for remote mobile access

question: Should OpenClaw core own an OAuth cloud relay, heartbeat, and mobile Gateway relay contract, and what trust/config model should govern it?
rationale: The codebase does not currently expose this capability, and adding it would create new remote ingress, persistent credentials, backend ownership, and config migration commitments that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design core relay first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor, approve the trust/config/storage model, then split implementation into small Gateway, CLI, mobile, and backend-contract PRs.

options.title: Defer to existing reachability paths
options.body: Reject or defer the relay direction and instead improve Tailscale, SSH, LAN, and QR/setup-code UX without adding cloud credentials or backend relay ownership.

options.title: Define extension seams only
options.body: Limit core work to missing plugin/API seams and require the hosted relay/backend package to live outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Design core relay first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor, approve the trust/config/storage model, then split implementation into small Gateway, CLI, mobile, and backend-contract PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history is on Gateway remote access, setup-code routing, and the relevant security docs, which are the decision surfaces this issue would change.
